INS number alone is insufficient to determine allergen status — manufacturer source confirmation required.

health_considerations.message: FDA nêu: benzen có thể hình thành ở mức rất thấp (ppb) trong một số đồ uống chứa đồng thời muối benzoat và acid ascorbic (vitamin C) hoặc acid erythorbic; nhiệt và ánh sáng có thể thúc đẩy quá trình này. Benzen là chất gây ung thư ở người.
health_considerations.note: Benzene formation risk when combined with ascorbic acid (INS 300) in acidic beverages (FDA 2006). Risk is conditional: only applies when product contains BOTH INS 211 and INS 300. Rule: derive CAUTION only when co-present with INS 300.
health_considerations.message_before_review: When co-formulated with ascorbic acid (vitamin C, INS 300) in beverages, sodium benzoate can produce trace amounts of benzene — a known IARC Group 1 carcinogen — particularly under heat and light exposure. Mechanism: benzoate → benzoic acid in acidic media; benzoic acid + ascorbic acid + trace metals (Fe²⁺/Cu²⁺) → hydroxyl radicals → benzene. FDA 2006 survey found benzene > 5 ppb in 10 beverages with both preservatives. Industry guidance: avoid co-formulating benzoate salts with ascorbic acid or erythorbic acid in beverages; if necessary, minimize heat and light exposure during storage. No legal limit for benzene in food; 5 ppb WHO drinking-water guideline used as a reference point.
health_considerations.review_note: Đã viết lại theo đúng văn bản nguồn đã lưu; số liệu/chi tiết không có trong nguồn đã bị bỏ.

allergen_assessment.note: Caramel nhóm IV sản xuất có hợp chất sulfit; phải khai báo khi lượng sulfit tồn dư trong thực phẩm đạt ngưỡng của danh mục. Sulfit có tên trong cả hai danh mục: Codex yêu cầu ghi khi từ 10 mg/kg trở lên; EU yêu cầu ghi khi trên 10 mg/kg hoặc 10 mg/lít (tính theo SO2 tổng, ở dạng sẵn sàng sử dụng). Không xác định được từ mã phụ gia, cần số liệu của sản phẩm.

allergen_assessment.note_before_review: Caramel Class IV (ammonia-sulfite process) may contain residual sulfites as a manufacturing by-product. The caramel additive itself is not a primary allergen, but if SO₂ carry-over in the final food product reaches ≥10 mg/kg, sulfite allergen labeling is triggered under Codex CXS 1-1985 and EU 1333/2008 carry-over limits. Product-level sulfite testing is required; cannot be determined from additive code alone.

sources.locator: IARC Monographs Vol. 101 classifies 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) as Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans) — evidence from lung tumours in mice; not in rats; genotoxicity data largely negative. E150d (Class IV, sulfite-ammonia caramel) produces 4-MEI as a manufacturing by-product of carbohydrate heating with sulfite + ammonium compounds. EU Regulation 1333/2008 sets maximum 4-MEI limits for Classes III and IV. California Prop 65 requires warning for beverages yielding > 29 μg 4-MEI equivalent/day. FDA position: typical dietary exposure far below tumour-causing doses in rodents.

health_considerations.message: Theo EFSA 2016, mẫn cảm với sulfit chủ yếu gặp ở người hen suyễn và có thể gặp ở số ít người không hen; ước tính 3–10% người hen nhạy cảm với sulfit. EFSA 2022 rút bỏ ADI tạm thời và dùng biên độ phơi nhiễm (MoE): MoE dưới 80 ở mọi nhóm dân số (phơi nhiễm percentile 95 cao nhất, kịch bản tinh chỉnh).
health_considerations.message_before_review: Sulfites trigger bronchospasm in an estimated 5–10% of chronic asthmatic patients (non-IgE mechanism: reflex bronchoconstriction or direct airway irritation). EFSA 2016 re-evaluation set a temporary group ADI pending further data on hypersensitivity reactions; EFSA 2022 withdrew the temporary ADI and adopted a Margin of Exposure (MoE) approach — MoE should be ≥80, but was found below 80 for high consumers across all age groups. Mandatory labeling at ≥10 mg/kg SO₂ in final product is specifically designed to protect this group.
health_considerations.review_note: Đã viết lại theo đúng văn bản nguồn đã lưu; số liệu/chi tiết không có trong nguồn đã bị bỏ.

evidence.quote: Sulfite sensitivity occurs mostly in asthmatics and may occur in a small number of non-asthmatic individuals.
It is estimated that 3–10% of all asthmatics are sensitive to sulfites.
MOEs at the maximum of 95th percentile ranges were below 80 for all population groups

health_considerations.message: Theo EFSA 2016, mẫn cảm với sulfit chủ yếu gặp ở người hen suyễn và có thể gặp ở số ít người không hen; ước tính 3–10% người hen nhạy cảm với sulfit. EFSA 2022 rút bỏ ADI tạm thời và dùng biên độ phơi nhiễm (MoE): MoE dưới 80 ở mọi nhóm dân số (phơi nhiễm percentile 95 cao nhất, kịch bản tinh chỉnh).
health_considerations.message_before_review: Sulfites trigger bronchospasm in an estimated 5–10% of chronic asthmatic patients (non-IgE mechanism: reflex bronchoconstriction or direct airway irritation). EFSA 2016 re-evaluation set a temporary group ADI pending further data on hypersensitivity reactions; EFSA 2022 withdrew the temporary ADI and adopted a Margin of Exposure (MoE) approach — MoE should be ≥80, but was found below 80 for high consumers across all age groups. Mandatory labeling at ≥10 mg/kg SO₂ in final product is specifically designed to protect this group.

KDOQI 2020 (khuyến nghị 6.3.2): khi quyết định hạn chế phospho, nên cân nhắc sinh khả dụng của nguồn phospho (động vật, thực vật, phụ gia).
health_considerations.message_before_review: Inorganic phosphate additives have ~90–100% intestinal absorption bioavailability, substantially higher than naturally occurring food phosphorus (animal 40–80%, plant 30%). KDOQI 2020 recommends restricting dietary phosphorus from processed food additives for CKD patients with hyperphosphatemia (stages 3b–5 and dialysis). Phosphate additives are not listed on nutrition labels in most countries, making them a 'hidden' source for patients managing phosphorus intake.
health_considerations.review_note: Đã viết lại theo đúng văn bản nguồn đã lưu; số liệu/chi tiết không có trong nguồn đã bị bỏ.

KDOQI 2020 (khuyến nghị 6.3.2): khi quyết định hạn chế phospho, nên cân nhắc sinh khả dụng của nguồn phospho (động vật, thực vật, phụ gia).
health_considerations.message_before_review: Inorganic phosphate additives have ~90–100% intestinal absorption bioavailability, substantially higher than naturally occurring food phosphorus (animal 40–80%, plant 30%). KDOQI 2020 recommends restricting dietary phosphorus from processed food additives for CKD patients with hyperphosphatemia (stages 3b–5 and dialysis). Phosphate additives are not listed on nutrition labels in most countries, making them a 'hidden' source for patients managing phosphorus intake.

KDOQI 2020 (khuyến nghị 6.3.2): khi quyết định hạn chế phospho, nên cân nhắc sinh khả dụng của nguồn phospho (động vật, thực vật, phụ gia).
health_considerations.message_before_review: Inorganic phosphate additives have ~90–100% intestinal absorption bioavailability, substantially higher than naturally occurring food phosphorus (animal 40–80%, plant 30%). KDOQI 2020 recommends restricting dietary phosphorus from processed food additives for CKD patients with hyperphosphatemia (stages 3b–5 and dialysis). Phosphate additives are not listed on nutrition labels in most countries, making them a 'hidden' source for patients managing phosphorus intake.

health_considerations.message_before_review: Sorbitol and other polyols cause osmotic diarrhoea, bloating, and abdominal cramping at high intake levels. Clinical threshold: > 20 g/day sorbitol from all sources. EU Regulation 1169/2011 (continuing Directive 94/54/EC): mandatory label 'excessive consumption may produce laxative effects' for foods containing > 10% added polyols. Commission Regulation 2021/1175 restricts polyol use in beverages due to laxative risk. High-risk scenario: heavy consumers of sugar-free confectionery, gum, or chocolate may accumulate > 20 g/day without realising it. Particularly relevant for children (lower body weight) and IBS patients.

health_considerations.message_before_review: Inorganic phosphate additives have ~90–100% intestinal absorption bioavailability, substantially higher than naturally occurring food phosphorus (animal 40–80%, plant 30%). KDOQI 2020 recommends restricting dietary phosphorus from processed food additives for CKD patients with hyperphosphatemia (stages 3b–5 and dialysis). Phosphate additives are not listed on nutrition labels in most countries, making them a 'hidden' source for patients managing phosphorus intake.
